jobs.title: Associate Director, Privacy, Data Protection and Information Governance
jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The Opportunity:

The risks in today’s disruptive environment are increasingly multifaced and evolve faster than ever before. We’re continuously evolving the ways we proactively manage risk to address the risk environment of tomorrow. EY Canada’s Risk Management (RM) function is responsible for the management of a variety of risks associated with regulation, data protection, client and engagement acceptance, conflicts, and independence.

Our highly engaged privacy and data protection team is looking to hire a data and information governance professional, with knowledge and experience in privacy and records and information management. As an integral part of the team, this individual will be directly involved with policies, processes and procedures established to maintain the Firm’s compliance with applicable privacy laws and regulations in Canada and records and information management standards. This individual will also serve as a role model by promoting and demonstrating commitment to risk management processes and policies within the Firm.

This job posting relates to an existing vacancy within our organization.

Key
Responsibilities:

Support and promote compliance with various data protection laws and regulations and EY policies and processes related to data protection and records and information management
Individual will be required to provide appropriate and effective solutions and to consistently provide high-quality risk-appropriate advice to professionals.
Measure and monitor the effectiveness of tools and processes, conduct regular monitoring and reporting, solicit feedback from stakeholders and recommend improvements.
Provide direct support to EY Canada’s Privacy and Data Protection Leader and the team.
Work with EY Global functions, other EY member firms, and local stakeholders to implement global policies, processes and tools within Canada. Manage other special projects on an as needed basis.
Support specialty practice areas in their compliance with specific data requirements.
Develop and deliver training to new hires and professional personnel, as required, and deploy data protection and records and information management awareness campaigns on a regular basis.

Skills and attributes for success:

Strong analytical, problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to exercise sound judgment and provide practical, risk-appropriate advice.
Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and changing deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability and willingness to educate and train others.
Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders across the organization.
Strong client-service orientation and the ability to handle difficult or demanding situations professionally.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment while managing sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
Ability to understand and interpret policies, standards and regulatory requirements and provide clear guidance to stakeholders.
Adaptability and flexibility to respond to evolving privacy, data governance and records and information management requirements.

To qualify for the role, you must have

A minimum of five years of experience in data protection, data/information governance, or records and information management.
Comprehensive and current knowledge of records and information management practices and standards, including classification systems, metadata standards, records retention, preservation and protection requirements.
Knowledge of Canadian federal and provincial privacy laws and an understanding of evolving privacy and data protection requirements.
Experience supporting the implementation, monitoring or improvement of data governance, records management, privacy or compliance-related policies and processes.
Knowledge and understanding of risk management and compliance principles, including experience interpreting policies and providing related guidance.
Project management experience or demonstrated experience managing data governance, records management, privacy or compliance-related initiatives.
Knowledge of, or experience working within, a multidisciplinary professional services environment would be an asset.
Knowledge of CASL, GDPR and California privacy requirements would be considered an asset.

What We Offer

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. In addition, our Total Rewards package allows you decide which benefits are right for you and which ones help you create a solid foundation for your future. Our Total Rewards package includes a discretionary bonus program, a comprehensive medical, prescription drug and dental coverage plan, a defined contribution pension plan, a great vacation policy plus firm paid days that allow you to enjoy longer long weekends throughout the year, statutory holidays and paid personal days (based on province of residence), and a range of exciting programs and benefits designed to support your physical, financial and social well-being. Plus, we offer:

Support and coaching from some of the most engaging colleagues in the industry
Learning opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that’s right for you

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To help create the best experience during the recruitment process, please describe any accommodations you may need.

Inclusiveness at EY

Inclusiveness is at the heart of who we are and how we work. We’re committed to fostering an environment where differences are valued, policies and practices are equitable, and our people feel a sense of belonging. We embrace diversity and are committed to combating systemic racism, advancing gender equity and women in leadership, advocating for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, promoting our neuroinclusion and accessibility initiatives, and are dedicated to amplifying the voices of Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis) nationally as we strive towards reconciliation. Our diverse experiences, abilities, backgrounds, and perspectives make our people unique and help guide us. Because when people feel free to be their authentic selves at work, they bring their best and are empowered to build a better working world.

Learn about our commitment to Inclusiveness at https://www.ey.com/en_ca/about-us/corporate-responsibility/equity

EY | Building a better working world

EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.

At EY, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools as one element of our recruitment process to enhance efficiency and improve the candidate experience. While AI supports us in our process, human judgment and decision-making remain integral in our candidate experience. We are committed to the responsible use of AI, and our practices are continuously reviewed and refined to ensure they align with ethical principles and regulatory requirements.

jobs.title: Director of Finance / Controller
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director of Finance / Controller to join LITCO LSO, a growing organization with multiple entities. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and partnering closely with the Fractional Chief Financial Officer, this role provides leadership to the Finance and Accounting team while overseeing accounting operations, financial reporting, budgeting, audit coordination and finance activities across multiple entities.

This role is responsible for strengthening the accounting function, improving financial reporting, and establishing consistent finance processes. The position also supports acquisition integration and the ongoing development of financial controls, reporting standards and accounting practices across the organization.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is an experienced finance leader with a strong technical accounting foundation and demonstrated success leading accounting and finance functions within complex, multi entity organizations. This individual combines strong financial management, budgeting, audit oversight, and financial reporting expertise with the ability to establish structure, improve processes, and strengthen financial controls.

Comfortable working with senior leaders and strong personalities, this individual provides objective advice, constructive challenge, and practical solutions. Success in the role requires confidence, resilience, sound judgment, executive presence, and the professional maturity to communicate candidly, uphold strong financial practices, and navigate complex situations with credibility.

THE ORGANIZATION

Litco LSO is North America’s leading Legal Support Organization, partnering with high-performing law firms that share our commitment to excellence, innovation, and client-first service. Backed by institutional investors and built on a foundation of operational rigor, we provide the resources, infrastructure, and strategic guidance firms need to scale—without sacrificing their values or autonomy. Our platform includes shared services in finance, HR, IT, marketing, and compliance, freeing our partner firms to focus on what they do best: serving clients.

We’re redefining what it means to run a modern law firm. Whether through M&A integration, advanced technology, or culture-driven leadership, Litco helps legal teams move beyond outdated business models and toward a sustainable, future-ready approach. Our growing network spans multiple jurisdictions across Canada and the U.S., uniting like-minded firms under a shared mission: to build the most respected and forward-thinking legal organization on the continent.

For more information, please visit their website: www.litcolso.com

RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Reporting & Accounting

Lead the organization’s accounting and financial reporting functions across multiple entities.
Oversee the preparation of consolidated financial statements and ensure consistent accounting practices.
Ensure the timely and accurate preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements.
Maintain effective accounting policies, controls and reporting standards.
Provide financial analysis and recommendations that support business performance and operational decision making.

Budgeting & Financial Planning

Lead the annual budgeting process and ongoing forecasting activities.
Monitor financial performance, analyze variances, and identify emerging risks and opportunities.
Lead monthly operating reviews with each business unit, partnering with executive leaders to review financial performance, budget variances, forecasts, and operational results in support of effective decision making.
Develop financial models and analysis to support planning, resource allocation, and organizational objectives.

Audit & Financial Oversight

Oversee the annual external audit process and act as the primary liaison with external auditors.
Coordinate audit planning, documentation, and the resolution of audit related matters.
Ensure financial policies, procedures, and controls are maintained and consistently applied.
Ensure compliance with applicable financial reporting, regulatory, and internal control requirements.

Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration

Support finance related activities associated with acquisitions and integrations.
Support finance due diligence and post acquisition integration activities, as required.
Assist in evaluating and integrating financial processes across acquired entities.
Promote consistency in financial reporting, controls, and accounting practices across multiple entities.

Systems & Process Improvement

Lead or support the implementation, optimization, and enhancement of financial systems and reporting tools.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and effectiveness within the finance function.
Support technology and process improvement initiatives that strengthen financial management and operational effectiveness.

Leadership & Stakeholder Collaboration

Provide leadership, direction, and mentorship to the Finance and Accounting team.
Build and strengthen the team through coaching, mentoring, and succession planning.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Build effective working relationships with senior leaders and key stakeholders.
Communicate financial information clearly, confidently and effectively to a variety of audiences.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
CPA designation required.
Strong technical accounting foundation with experience preparing consolidated financial statements.
Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in finance and accounting, including experience leading finance and accounting functions within a complex organization.
Demonstrated experience overseeing budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and year end audit activities.
Experience working within organizations that operate across multiple entities, business units, or corporate structures.
Demonstrated experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, and integration activities.
Experience leading and developing finance and accounting teams.
Experience supporting financial systems implementations, technology-enabled process improvements, or organizational transformation initiatives is considered an asset.
Strong understanding of accounting principles, financial reporting, financial controls, and financial management practices.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Demonstrates strong financial and business acumen, using analysis and sound judgment to support effective organizational decision making.
Communicates with confidence, credibility, and executive presence, effectively presenting financial information, recommendations and business insights to senior leaders and C-suite executives.
Builds trusted relationships and provides objective advice and constructive challenge, demonstrating the confidence and professional maturity to work effectively with senior leaders, strong personalities, and diverse stakeholder groups.
Exercises professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment when managing sensitive issues and competing priorities.
Leads teams through accountability, mentorship, and clear expectations, fostering a culture of engagement and performance.
Identifies opportunities to improve processes, strengthen controls, and enhance operational effectiveness.
Comfortable establishing structure and adapting to changing priorities in a growing organization.
Adapts effectively to changing priorities and organizational needs while maintaining a practical, solutions focused approach.
Demonstrates integrity, accountability, and professionalism in all aspects of leadership and financial stewardship.

FOR MORE INFORMATION, PLEASE CONTACT

jobs.title: Director, Strategic Finance - Remote in Canada
jobs.description:
DIRECTOR, STRATEGIC FINANCE

Who is a Director, Strategic Finance?

The Director, Strategic Finance is a high-impact leader within the Office of the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) who brings an investment-oriented perspective to GoodLife Group’s most consequential strategic, financial and enterprise-value decisions. This role personally leads complex analysis and selected cross-functional workstreams under the delegated authority of the CFO.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, the role expands the capacity and analytical depth of the Office of the CFO across executive decision support, capital allocation, enterprise performance, Value Creation Plan validation, Apollo and Board engagement, financing and merger and acquisition (M&A) execution.

Working with leadership from across Financial Planning & Analysis, Accounting, Data & Analytics and Operations departments, the role influences through expertise, credibility and delegated CFO authority, while functional leaders retain ownership of their teams, source information and recurring processes.

What will you be doing?

Enterprise strategic finance, corporate modelling and capital allocation

Build, enhance and apply integrated financial models, strategic scenarios and sensitivity analyses that connect operating performance, cash flow, leverage, capital requirements, and enterprise value.
Evaluate organic growth initiatives, capital projects, acquisitions, financing alternatives and other uses of capital through disciplined return, risk, liquidity and enterprise-value analysis; establish appropriate post investment performance reviews.
Translate complex financial, operational and market information into clear alternatives, trade-offs and recommendations for the CFO, CEO, and executive leadership.

Apollo, Board and lender performance insight

Lead the financial synthesis, analytical challenge and development of decision-useful performance narratives for selected Apollo, Board and lender discussions, while the CFO remains the primary relationship owner and existing teams retain responsibility for underlying financial information.
Integrate and constructively challenge inputs from Financial Planning & Analysis, Accounting, Data & Analytics and operating teams to identify key drivers, emerging risks, outlook implications and required decisions
Partner with the CFO and executive leadership to articulate clear financial narratives regarding business performance, strategic priorities, risks, and opportunities.
Lead selected follow-up analyses and coordinate timely resolution of material questions, commitments and decisions arising from Apollo, Board and lender discussions.

M&A, financing and strategic transaction execution

Lead core financial analysis and selected execution workstreams for acquisitions, dispositions, refinancing's and other strategic transactions, including screening, valuation, financial modelling, due diligence, scenario analysis and approval materials.
Support the CFO in evaluating capital structure, liquidity requirements, financing alternatives, and capital-allocation priorities.
Coordinate Finance workstreams, data-room requirements and financial analysis across internal teams, financing sources, counterparties and external advisors.
Evaluate transaction structures, synergies, risks, integration considerations and value-creation implications, and support post transaction performance tracking where appropriate.

Executive decision support and Office of the CFO effectiveness

Serve as a trusted thought partner to the CFO on high-priority strategic, financial and operational matters.
Lead selected cross-functional strategic workstreams and high-priority analyses, bringing investment discipline, structure, pace and clear accountability to complex or ambiguous issues.
Support the financial elements of the Value Creation Plan, including connecting initiative impacts to the long-range financial model, validating material financial assumptions and supporting the reporting cadence for key financial and operating KPIs, without assuming ownership of broader VCP governance or initiative execution.
Institutionalize rigorous decision and review processes for priority Office of the CFO mandates, including clear accountabilities, analytical standards and escalation protocols.
Build trusted relationships with long-tenured leaders and ensure that Strategic Finance complements, rather than cuts across, the responsibilities of existing functional teams.

Do you have what it takes?

Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics, accounting, mathematics, engineering or another quantitatively rigorous discipline
4 to 7 years of progressively responsible experience in private equity, investment banking, pension or infrastructure investing, strategic finance or another analytically rigorous transaction- or investment-oriented environment.
Demonstrated experience building and interpreting complex financial models, evaluating investments or transactions, and preparing concise decision materials for senior executives, investment committees, Boards or equivalent senior stakeholders
Advanced financial modelling, valuation, investment-return analysis, scenario analysis and business-case development skills, with expert-level proficiency in Microsoft Excel and the ability to create concise, executive-quality PowerPoint materials.
Deep understanding of the connections among income statement performance, balance sheet requirements, cash flow, liquidity, leverage, covenants and enterprise value.
Exceptional analytical judgment and attention to detail, with the ability to identify inconsistencies, test assumptions, distinguish material issues from noise and reconcile information from multiple sources.
Exceptional written, verbal and presentation communication skills, including the ability to produce concise, persuasive, executive- and Board-quality materials.
Credibility, judgment, and executive presence to work directly with senior leaders, investors, lenders and advisors while handling confidential information appropriately.
Highly self-directed, organized and action oriented; able to manage multiple workstreams, tight deadlines and ambiguity without requiring a large team or extensive direction.
A hands-on orientation and willingness to move between high-level strategic questions and detailed analysis and execution.
Strong collaboration and influencing skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional work through expertise, credibility and delegated authority rather than formal hierarchy.
Intellectual curiosity and a genuine interest in understanding GoodLife’s businesses at the club, member and operating-process levels.

What’s in it for you?

Ongoing training & development to ensure a long & successful career path
Career advancement opportunities
Competitive Total Rewards Package
FREE Performance Fitness membership
Fun & energetic atmosphere to come to every day!

At GoodLife Fitness, we are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees & members feel valued, respected & supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers & communities in which we live & serve. We are committed to meeting the accessibility needs of persons with disabilities in a manner that respects their dignity & that is equitable. If you require an accommodation for the recruitment/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, accessible meeting rooms or other accommodation), please let us know & we will work with you to meet your needs.

Compensation:

It is expected that the selected candidate will start at a base salary of $131,000. This position is eligible for bonuses in addition to the base salary. The annual range of expected compensation for the position is $146,000 - $196,000 determined by performance, time in the position and variable compensation earned.

jobs.description:
About The Opportunity

Our internationally recognized, growing client in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) is seeking a forward-thinking Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join their team on a full-time, permanent basis.

This opportunity joins a progressive organization that offers professional growth and development while being a key player within the Senior Leadership team. The CFO will lead Finance functions and provide leadership to the Finance & Accounting team, creating a positive, optimal experience as growth continues both locally, nationally, and on the international stage.

Duties include but are not limited to:

Strategic Financial Leadership

Partner with the CEO to develop and execute the company's long-term growth strategy
Lead enterprise-wide financial planning, forecasting, capital allocation, and performance management
Provide strategic guidance on expansion initiatives, manufacturing investments, capacity planning, and operational efficiency
Support business development, commercial growth, and international expansion opportunities

Financial Planning and Analysis:

Develop and implement financial strategies, plans, and budgets aligned with the company's goals and objectives
Conduct financial analysis, forecasting, and modeling to evaluate performance and identify opportunities for improvement
Monitor key financial metrics and provide regular reporting to senior management
Lead the annual budgeting process and long-term financial planning efforts
Identify opportunities for cost optimization and revenue enhancement to drive profitability

Mergers, Acquisitions & Corporate Development

Develop and execute an acquisition strategy aligned with the company's growth objectives, evaluate strategic partnerships
Drive integration efforts to maximize operational efficiencies and financial returns
Manage capital allocation decisions, including capital expenditures, investments, and financing activities as needed
Lead equity raises, debt financings, and other capital markets transactions
Demonstrate strong understanding of IPO readiness and execution, including financial reporting, governance, internal controls, and investor communications
Build and maintain strong relationships with investors, lenders, and other external stakeholders- effectively communicate the company's growth story and value proposition
Serve as a key liaison with financial institutions, regulatory agencies, and external auditors
Communicate financial performance, forecasts, and strategic initiatives to the executive team and external stakeholders
Optimize the company's capital structure and liquidity position to support growth and operational needs
Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and board on financial matters and strategic decisions

Manufacturing & Operational Finance

Provide financial leadership across manufacturing operations, supply chain management, procurement, inventory management, and distribution
Drive improvements in gross margin, operational efficiency, working capital, and cash flow performance
Establish financial metrics and reporting systems to support manufacturing and operational decision-making
Evaluate capital expenditure investments, facility expansions, automation initiatives, and production optimization programs
Support strategic sourcing and supply chain resilience initiatives

Regulatory, Compliance & Risk Management

Ensure compliance with all applicable financial, healthcare, and manufacturing regulations, implement effective internal controls and compliance programs to safeguard assets and mitigate risks
Oversee financial infrastructure, including SOX compliance and reporting processes
Maintain strong internal controls, governance practices, and enterprise risk management frameworks
Partner with internal and external auditors to maintain high compliance standards
Stay abreast of changes in financial regulations and industry trends to ensure compliance as well as assess and manage financial risks, including credit, market, and operational risks

Financial Operations

Oversee all aspects of financial operations, including accounting, budgeting, treasury, and tax compliance
Oversee Finance & Accounting team, providing leadership, direction, and fostering a collaborative culture and continuous improvement
Prepare accurate and timely financial statements and reports for management and external stakeholders
Ensure timely, accurate, and transparent financial reporting to management, investors, and external stakeholders
Ensure compliance with accounting standards, regulatory requirements, and internal policies
Mentor and develop finance professionals, promoting skill development and career growth within the organization

About You

The successful candidate will have the following:

CPA Designation, Active in Good Standing
Proven experience in a senior financial leadership role, with 5+ years at an executive level
Strong understanding of financial principles, accounting standards and practices, IPOs, Mergers & Acquisitions, and regulatory requirements
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex financial data and make strategic recommendations
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively with internal and external stakeholders
Demonstrated leadership ability, with a track record of building high-performing teams and driving results
Strategic mindset, with the ability to think creatively and contribute to overall business strategy and growth initiatives

Please apply by clicking the “Apply Now” button below and follow the instructions to submit your résumé. You can also apply by submitting your résumé directly to sgomi@lrostaffing.com. If you are already registered with us, please contact your Senior Recruiter. Please quote job 19222

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Global Transaction Banking

Global Transaction Banking (GTB) is the payments and transaction engine of Scotiabank. We support Small Business, Commercial and Corporate clients with effective treasury management solutions coupled with a best-in-class service model, making it easy for clients to do business with us.

As businesses build their digital capabilities and transform their operating models, their payment needs are evolving too. Boasting a unique global footprint, GTB’s comprehensive suite of innovative banking solutions help our business clients generate operational efficiencies, streamline and simplify payments, improve working capital performance, and mitigate financial risk.

At Scotiabank, we embrace your strengths, ideas, and ambitions. GTB is a fast-growing team with a focus on the Americas, particularly Canada, the U.S., Mexico, and we are seeking top tier talent to complement our organization.

Join a purpose-driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Purpose

The Trade Finance Operations Manager plays a pivotal role in leading and overseeing end-to-end trade finance operations, ensuring the accurate and efficient execution of trade finance transactions across the full transaction lifecycle. The role requires strong expertise in trade finance products, sound managerial capability, and a strategic mindset to support seamless delivery, strong stakeholder engagement, and compliance with governing regulations, internal policies, and procedures.

What You'll Do

Leads assessment of opportunities for Global Transaction Banking from a strategy and product vision, customer experience, delivery, business case, and industry perspective; responsible for providing critical business recommendations to GTB executive team. Projects include a mix of product-focused projects (e.g., evaluating new payment innovations) as well as region-focused projects (e.g., GTM strategy in a particular Scotiabank market or region).
Serves as a strategic advisor for GTB leadership team on competitive intelligence, operating model design, best practices, setting of objectives and key results (OKRs), and end-to-end coordination of strategic initiatives across the business (Product, Operations, Sales, Technology, etc.).

Minimum 8+ years of experience in management consulting and/or in comparable enterprise strategy role with either a financial institution or fintech.

Comfort with translating a strategic topic into a Board-level business plan and strategy end-to-end, working with internal and external stakeholders.

new_jobs.description:
About The Opportunity

Our internationally recognized, growing client in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) is seeking a forward-thinking Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join their team on a full-time, permanent basis.

This opportunity joins a progressive organization that offers professional growth and development while being a key player within the Senior Leadership team. The CFO will lead Finance functions and provide leadership to the Finance & Accounting team, creating a positive, optimal experience as growth continues both locally, nationally, and on the international stage.

Duties include but are not limited to:

Strategic Financial Leadership

Partner with the CEO to develop and execute the company's long-term growth strategy
Lead enterprise-wide financial planning, forecasting, capital allocation, and performance management
Provide strategic guidance on expansion initiatives, manufacturing investments, capacity planning, and operational efficiency
Support business development, commercial growth, and international expansion opportunities

Financial Planning and Analysis:

Develop and implement financial strategies, plans, and budgets aligned with the company's goals and objectives
Conduct financial analysis, forecasting, and modeling to evaluate performance and identify opportunities for improvement
Monitor key financial metrics and provide regular reporting to senior management
Lead the annual budgeting process and long-term financial planning efforts
Identify opportunities for cost optimization and revenue enhancement to drive profitability

Mergers, Acquisitions & Corporate Development

Develop and execute an acquisition strategy aligned with the company's growth objectives, evaluate strategic partnerships
Drive integration efforts to maximize operational efficiencies and financial returns
Manage capital allocation decisions, including capital expenditures, investments, and financing activities as needed
Lead equity raises, debt financings, and other capital markets transactions
Demonstrate strong understanding of IPO readiness and execution, including financial reporting, governance, internal controls, and investor communications
Build and maintain strong relationships with investors, lenders, and other external stakeholders- effectively communicate the company's growth story and value proposition
Serve as a key liaison with financial institutions, regulatory agencies, and external auditors
Communicate financial performance, forecasts, and strategic initiatives to the executive team and external stakeholders
Optimize the company's capital structure and liquidity position to support growth and operational needs
Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and board on financial matters and strategic decisions

Manufacturing & Operational Finance

Provide financial leadership across manufacturing operations, supply chain management, procurement, inventory management, and distribution
Drive improvements in gross margin, operational efficiency, working capital, and cash flow performance
Establish financial metrics and reporting systems to support manufacturing and operational decision-making
Evaluate capital expenditure investments, facility expansions, automation initiatives, and production optimization programs
Support strategic sourcing and supply chain resilience initiatives

Regulatory, Compliance & Risk Management

Ensure compliance with all applicable financial, healthcare, and manufacturing regulations, implement effective internal controls and compliance programs to safeguard assets and mitigate risks
Oversee financial infrastructure, including SOX compliance and reporting processes
Maintain strong internal controls, governance practices, and enterprise risk management frameworks
Partner with internal and external auditors to maintain high compliance standards
Stay abreast of changes in financial regulations and industry trends to ensure compliance as well as assess and manage financial risks, including credit, market, and operational risks

Financial Operations

Oversee all aspects of financial operations, including accounting, budgeting, treasury, and tax compliance
Oversee Finance & Accounting team, providing leadership, direction, and fostering a collaborative culture and continuous improvement
Prepare accurate and timely financial statements and reports for management and external stakeholders
Ensure timely, accurate, and transparent financial reporting to management, investors, and external stakeholders
Ensure compliance with accounting standards, regulatory requirements, and internal policies
Mentor and develop finance professionals, promoting skill development and career growth within the organization

About You

The successful candidate will have the following:

CPA Designation, Active in Good Standing
Proven experience in a senior financial leadership role, with 5+ years at an executive level
Strong understanding of financial principles, accounting standards and practices, IPOs, Mergers & Acquisitions, and regulatory requirements
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex financial data and make strategic recommendations
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively with internal and external stakeholders
Demonstrated leadership ability, with a track record of building high-performing teams and driving results
Strategic mindset, with the ability to think creatively and contribute to overall business strategy and growth initiatives

How To Apply

Please apply by clicking the “Apply Now” button below and follow the instructions to submit your résumé. You can also apply by submitting your résumé directly to sgomi@lrostaffing.com. If you are already registered with us, please contact your Senior Recruiter. Please quote job 19222
.

Each submission is reviewed by an experienced recruiter to ensure a thoughtful and equitable evaluation of every candidate.

Requisition ID: 274835

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Global Transaction Banking

Global Transaction Banking (GTB) is the payments and transaction engine of Scotiabank. We support Small Business, Commercial and Corporate clients with effective treasury management solutions coupled with a best-in-class service model, making it easy for clients to do business with us.

As businesses build their digital capabilities and transform their operating models, their payment needs are evolving too. Boasting a unique global footprint, GTB’s comprehensive suite of innovative banking solutions help our business clients generate operational efficiencies, streamline and simplify payments, improve working capital performance, and mitigate financial risk.

At Scotiabank, we embrace your strengths, ideas, and ambitions. GTB is a fast-growing team with a focus on the Americas, particularly Canada, the U.S., Mexico, and we are seeking top tier talent to complement our organization.

Join a purpose-driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Purpose

The Trade Finance Operations Manager plays a pivotal role in leading and overseeing end-to-end trade finance operations, ensuring the accurate and efficient execution of trade finance transactions across the full transaction lifecycle. The role requires strong expertise in trade finance products, sound managerial capability, and a strategic mindset to support seamless delivery, strong stakeholder engagement, and compliance with governing regulations, internal policies, and procedures.

What You'll Do

Leads assessment of opportunities for Global Transaction Banking from a strategy and product vision, customer experience, delivery, business case, and industry perspective; responsible for providing critical business recommendations to GTB executive team. Projects include a mix of product-focused projects (e.g., evaluating new payment innovations) as well as region-focused projects (e.g., GTM strategy in a particular Scotiabank market or region).
Serves as a strategic advisor for GTB leadership team on competitive intelligence, operating model design, best practices, setting of objectives and key results (OKRs), and end-to-end coordination of strategic initiatives across the business (Product, Operations, Sales, Technology, etc.).
Engage and build relationships with stakeholders across Product, Technology, Design, Analytics, Operations, Risk, Controls, Finances, and the Lines of Business to influence change agenda.
Creates an environment in which his/her team pursues effective and efficient operations of his/her respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank's Values, its Code of Conduct and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.
Leads a high performance team and implements a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops and motivates their team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviors; communicating vision/values/business strategy; and, managing succession and development planning for the team.

What You'll Bring

Minimum 8+ years of experience in management consulting and/or in comparable enterprise strategy role with either a financial institution or fintech.
Demonstrated relationship and partner management skills, with a client focus that carries demonstrated experience and professionalism in client facing situations
Adept at strategic planning including leading scoping activities and developing approaches for opportunity development and assessment
Deep payments expertise and acumen; well versed in both business and technology to serve as an efficient liaison between business strategy functions and key stakeholders
Expertise leading, recruiting, and managing a high-performing team Strong business analysis skills and data-focused approach to business case development, including financial opportunity assessments and client needs analysis
Comfort with translating a strategic topic into a Board-level business plan and strategy end-to-end, working with internal and external stakeholders.

Working Conditions

Work in a standard office-based environment; non-standard hours might occur from time to time

Interested?

If your experience is closely related but doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification, we do encourage you to apply - you might be the right candidate for this or other roles at Scotiabank!

At Scotiabank, every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are and, embraced for their differences. That’s why we work to grow and diversify talent and engage employees in a performance-oriented culture.

Scotiabank wants you to be able to bring your best self to work – and life, every day. With a focus on holistic well-being, our many flexible benefit programs are designed to help support your unique family, financial, physical, mental, and social health needs.
